newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM H1 net seen higher but outlook poor.
newsitem.headline: KLM H1 net seen higher but outlook poor.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM may well downgrade its full-year earnings forecast on Tuesday, despite posting a jump in net profits over the first 1996/97 half, analysts predicted on Friday.
Net profits for the six months to September 30 are seen climbing to between 457 and 639 million guilders ($375.8 million) from a year-earlier 437 million guilders.
But analysts noted that around 377 million guilders of this would come from the sale and revaluation of KLM's preferred shareholding in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines.
Operating profits would come in much lower than in the year-earlier period, pressured by rising fuel costs, a higher wage bill and cut-throat market competition, they said.
"I do not think they can meet their full-year target," said Richard Brakenhoff, analyst at merchant bank MeesPierson.
"They would do well to adjust their earnings forecast," agreed Generale Bank's Corne Zandbergen.
KLM said in August full-year 1996/97 net profits would roughly equal the previous year's 547 million guilders.
But it cautioned operating profits for 1996/97 would be slightly down on their year-earlier equivalents.

Brakenhoff sees KLM first-half net profit surging to 566 million guilders in the first 1996/97 half from a year-earlier 437 million. Operating profits will drop to 321 million guilders from a year-earlier 497 million, he said.
In the traditionally strong second quarter, he sees operating profits sliding to 241 million guilders from a year-earlier 333 million.
"I estimate fuel costs will have picked up by some 34 percent and salaries by around 11 percent," he said.
Generale's Zandbergen said he saw first half net profit of 516 million guilders and operating profits of 241 million.
"If my estimates prove correct, I will definitely consider lowering my full-year earnings per share forecast," he added.
The bottom-line contribution from Northwest prefs would fall away in the second half, he noted.

KLM can start booking its share of Northwest profits once the U.S. airline returns to positive shareholders' equity (in early 1997) but this would amount to 200 million guilders a year at most, Zandbergen said.
